To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) CoSi provides a scalable, efficient, and privacy-preserving witness cosigning scheme that can be used to protect authorities from undetected compromise, 2) CoSi can be implemented in practice, and 3) CoSi is effective against a variety of attacks, including those that compromise a large number of witnesses and those that control a victim's internet access.

CoSi is the first practical, scalable protocol for transparently verifying the integrity of critical authorities, including name, time, certificate, and code signing services, by using collective signatures of diverse witnesses.

CoSi is an efficient and scalable witness cosignature protocol that enables a diverse group of distributed witnesses to collectively sign and publicly log authoritative statements, such as time and software updates, to ensure that the statements cannot be used to attack the system without detection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of protecting the security of a system from the inside.
protecting authorities and their clients against the risk of undetected compromise of critical network infrastructure.
the design of a protocol that enables the public to verify the integrity of critical network authorities, such as time, certificate, and logging services.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

CoSi is an efficient, scalable, decentralized, and privacy-preserving witness cosigning scheme that can be used by a variety of applications, and that can be implemented using existing cryptographic primitives.
CoSi provides the first practical solution for protecting the privacy and integrity of critical network services against persistent attackers who control the authority and several witnesses.
CoSi is a scalable, privacy-preserving, and publicly-verifiable witness cosigning mechanism that can be applied to any authority that needs to be protected against persistent attackers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are building a system that allows a set of people to sign a message together, without having to meet in person or even know one another.

CoSi provides a scalable, efficient, and privacy-preserving mechanism to protect authorities and their users from undetected compromise, and thus to protect users' security from undetected authority compromise.
it provides a new way to protect authorities from being compromised by hackers or spy agencies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the security of critical authorities can be significantly improved by a small number of independent parties willing to publicly validate their actions.
the secret keys of critical authorities can be protected from compromise and misuse by forcing them to operate in the full light of public scrutiny.

, by combining cryptographic multisignatures with scalable communication structures, we can protect clients from undetected compromises of authorities and their witnesses, without compromising clients' privacy, without requiring any communication, and without any additional trust assumptions.
